source_name: MoneyGet bankomati Crna Gora — partner acquisition site
why_relevant: Local-language site recruiting Montenegrin merchants/locations as MoneyGet ATM hosts. Reveals the commercial model, expansion intent and site-type targeting of independent ATM deployment in ME — a leading indicator of where the cash network is growing while bank branches shrink.

source_name: Payten d.o.o. Podgorica — Montenegro legal entity (contact/recruitment footprint)
why_relevant: Confirms Payten operates a registered Montenegrin subsidiary (Serdara Jola Piletića 3A, Podgorica; asseco-see.me email domain) and its job ads (ATM/POS field-maintenance subcontractors, ATM deployment coordinators) are a proxy signal for estate size and expansion. Hiring pattern is an indirect read on terminal fleet growth. Also points to the legacy asseco-see.me domain as a further target.

Montenegro's specialist banking trade portal republishes vendor and scheme press releases verbatim and maintains per-vendor tag archives. It is the single best local-language aggregation point for supplier-ecosystem announcements (Payten job ads, CKB GO POS/Tap-to-Phone launch with Mastercard and Visa, Erste's first contactless ATM cash withdrawal in ME) that never reach the vendors' English sites.

source_name: AllSecure — payment gateway coverage / merchant support (Western Balkans acquiring)
why_relevant: AllSecure is the e-commerce gateway operating in Montenegro; its coverage and services pages describe its acquiring partnerships in the Western Balkans and the card brands supported. Establishes who technically enables card-not-present acceptance in ME and against which acquirer.

source_name: Montenegrin merchant checkout / payment-conditions pages naming gateway + acquirer
why_relevant: ME merchants are contractually obliged to disclose their card-processing chain on checkout/payment-terms pages, e.g. 'card payments realised in cooperation with AllSecure d.o.o. and Hipotekarna banka'. Systematically harvesting these boilerplate disclosures across ME merchant sites yields a bottom-up map of e-commerce acquirer and gateway market share that no regulator publishes.

source_name: Halcom — support/documentation and country e-banking manuals (Hal E-Bank, Halcom One)
why_relevant: Halcom supplies corporate e-banking and qualified e-signature infrastructure across ex-Yugoslav markets. Its per-bank manuals and support pages (published per client bank, per country) are a pointer to which banks run Hal E-Bank, and Halcom One marketing states the count of banks served per market — a proxy for corporate payments infrastructure concentration. No Montenegro-specific announcement was located in this pass.

source_name: Adriatic Bank — Mastercard membership and Apple Pay launch announcements
why_relevant: Bank-side announcements co-authored with the scheme: a new acquiring AND issuing Mastercard principal member in ME (a rare, datable change in the ME acquiring market structure) and a first Apple Pay rollout. Scheme-milestone news often appears on the issuer site before, or instead of, the scheme's own newsroom.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore — saopštenja (scheme co-branded programme rules)
why_relevant: Local-language issuer announcement of a Mastercard-run national e-commerce cashback programme ('Pay&Get') for all Mastercard cardholders in Montenegro, including mechanism and rules. Scheme-driven market-stimulation campaigns of this kind are datable evidence of e-commerce push and of scheme country-programme activity in ME.

source_name: Erste Bank Crna Gora — blog and contactless ATM cash withdrawal milestone
why_relevant: Erste ME reportedly first in Montenegro to deploy contactless cash withdrawal across its ATM network — an ATM-vendor-capability milestone that dates a fleet upgrade and implies the hardware/software generation of that estate. Its consumer blog also explains card-scheme differences, useful for glossary and local terminology.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — e-commerce / acquiring pages (AllSecure + Payten SoftPOS client)
why_relevant: Hipotekarna is the ME acquirer named by both AllSecure (gateway partner) and Payten (SoftPOS implementation) — the convergence point of the ME e-commerce and terminal supplier chain. Its corporate acquiring pages identify the technology partners it fronts and are the best single bank-side confirmation of the vendor map.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf — investor/press materials on ATM-as-a-Service and regional partnerships
why_relevant: Diebold Nixdorf (post Wincor merger) is one of the two dominant ATM hardware vendors whose machines populate SEE bank fleets; its newsroom and investor materials announce ATM-as-a-Service and regional deals. No Montenegro-specific announcement was found in this pass, so this is a monitoring target rather than a confirmed ME data source.

source_name: Payten regional launch coverage in SEE tech/business press (PC Press, Biznis i Finansije)
why_relevant: Regional Serbian-language tech and business press carries detailed Payten product interviews (Android POS terminals, Live UTMS remote terminal management) that describe the terminal technology being rolled out across the group's markets including Montenegro. Useful for dating the technology generation of ME terminal estates when vendor PR is country-silent.

source_name: CDM.me — republication of MasterIndex Crna Gora findings
why_relevant: Mainstream ME news portal that republishes MasterIndex results with headline percentages. Serves as a redundancy/backup channel if the Mastercard country page is restructured or an edition is delisted, and often carries figures in a plain-text form easier to extract than the scheme's own layout.

source_name: Mastercard Crna Gora official Facebook page (@MastercardCG)
why_relevant: The scheme's ME country social channel is often where campaign, milestone and MasterIndex teasers appear first and where items dropped from the website persist. Low evidential weight but high recency; useful as a tripwire for new scheme activity in ME.
